::: {.why}
The reproducibility gap you found last night is the difference between a platform and a collection of notebooks, and it is what milestone 5 is actually graded on.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Reproduce any reported result with one command from a clean checkout.
- Have every result record the code version, the configuration and the data snapshot that produced it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the entry point: a command taking a configuration file and producing a result object, with the git commit, the configuration hash and the store's ingestion cutoff recorded inside the result. Then rerun every milestone number through it and check each matches what you reported.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Fix the gaps you find. The usual ones are a hard-coded date, a parameter that lives in a notebook rather than in the configuration, and a data pull that has since changed. Each one you fix is a claim in milestone 5 that becomes true.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Every result is reproducible from a configuration file and a commit hash with one command, and each result records the code version and data cutoff that produced it. This is the property that makes the platform worth showing to someone.
:::
